claims.explanation: Atorvastatin's selective killing likely reflects dependence on the mevalonate/cholesterol synthesis pathway, with sensitive lines showing low baseline HMGCR-pathway activity or compensatory reliance on geranylgeranyl/isoprenoid-dependent survival signaling. The pattern is enriched for RAS/RTK-MAPK-activated and chromatin-remodeling-mutant lines, suggesting that statin-induced loss of prenylation or cholesterol intermediates preferentially kills cells with these dependencies. Resistance in several breast, mesothelioma, and KRAS/PIK3CA-mutant lines may reflect alternative survival signaling or lower dependence on HMGCR flux.

features.basis: atorvastatin directly inhibits HMGCR and statin-class transcriptional response is HMGCR-dependent
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with MAPK/RTK dependence on isoprenoid signaling
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK and appears in multiple sensitive lines
EGFR-mutant lung/CNS lines are among sensitive lines, suggesting RTK-driven dependence
SMARCA4-mutant lines are enriched in the sensitive set, possibly via chromatin-state dependence on mevalonate metabolites
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not sufficient; however, wild-type TP53 lines are not enriched among sensitive lines
KRAS-mutant lung/pancreas lines appear among least affected, suggesting KRAS-driven tumors may use alternative prenylation/survival routes
PIK3CA-mutant breast/ovary/gastric lines are enriched among resistant lines, consistent with PI3K-driven survival bypass
PTEN loss appears in resistant lines, suggesting PI3K/AKT activation reduces statin sensitivity
ARID1A-mutant lines appear in both groups but several resistant lines carry ARID1A mutations
NF2-mutant mesothelioma lines are among least affected, suggesting Hippo-pathway activation may protect
STK11-mutant lung/ovary lines appear among sensitive lines, possibly via metabolic stress vulnerability
